gaps.explanation: Statement = GAAP governmental funds statement (pp5-6) Total revenues 11,556,294. Detail = budgetary-basis schedules (pp13-17, headed 'Budget and Actual (Budgetary Basis)') for the five major funds plus the GAAP nonmajor combining statement (pp18-19). Per fund, GAAP (p5-6) vs budgetary actual: General 4,077,579 vs 4,077,585 (-6); Keno 1,772,842 vs 1,755,151 (+17,691); Street 2,126,794 vs 2,063,098 (+63,696); LB 840 525,693 vs 495,231 (+30,462); Downtown Development 519,462 vs 519,794 (-332); Nonmajor 2,533,924 vs 2,533,924 (0). -6 + 17,691 + 63,696 + 30,462 - 332 = 111,511 = gap. Every schedule line is in detail; the budgetary fund balances also differ from GAAP (e.g. General end of year 3,353,724 p13 vs 3,254,228 p5), so the schedules really print another basis. No fix.

Statement GAAP Total expenditures 11,660,624 (p6) vs budgetary schedules (pp13-17) + nonmajor combining (pp18-19). Per fund GAAP vs budgetary: General 5,994,878 vs 5,735,896 (+258,982; GAAP includes capital outlay 273,210, incl. the 224,525 lease issuance, which the budgetary schedule p13 does not print as a line); Keno 1,664,044 vs 1,671,336 (-7,292); Street 1,777,134 vs 1,802,987 (-25,853); LB 840 157,210 vs 156,343 (+867); Downtown Development 20,045 vs 20,045 (0); Nonmajor 2,047,313 vs 2,047,313 (0). 258,982 - 7,292 - 25,853 + 867 = 226,704 = gap. No fix.
